rationale: Greek loanword πληγή. Used here in the medical-pathological register paired with ⲓⲁⲃⲉ 'disease' and ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'sickness.'
Crum 192b 'poison, gall.' Pairs with ⲭⲟⲗⲏ 'gall' as toxic humors. The plural ⲙⲉⲧⲟⲩ supports vocalic plural marking.
Agent-noun: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who') + ϣⲟⲩⲟ ('pour out'). Standard agentive formation. Names a medicine that purges/evacuates.
Literally 'that-of-the-bone' (ⲡⲁⲧ- relational + ⲕⲉⲥ 'bone'). First (innermost) layer in the seven-part anatomical schema preceding the bone proper.
Greek loanword φορεῖν 'wear (clothing).' Lycopolitan ⲣ̄ϩⲟⲣⲉ = ⲣⲫⲟⲣⲉ in glossary; here 'wears the three garments upon his body.'
Recurring parable verb (lines 5, 6, 7) — the wise physician 'finds' antidote, purgative, soother. Lycopolitan verb of unclear root; functions as 'find/apply.' Worth flagging across pages.
Verbal noun of unclear root (possibly ϣⲱⲛⲥ 'plunder' or ϣⲱⲛϯ 'wrath'). The Living Spirit's act of expelling the three deceits from the archons.
Likely Lyc. reflex of ⲗⲱⲕϩ̄ 'sweet, soft' verbalized — the third medicine soothes the blows/wounds.
Verbal noun from ⲧⲁⲗϭⲟ 'heal.' Used twice on this page (lines 12, 19-20): 'medicine of the healing.'
